title: OKR Escalation Matrix + Reserve Capacity Playbook (company-level initiative hedging)
creator: Asha Nair
description:
Problem: Company-level objectives have tight critical paths across multiple teams (Runtime, Console, Dedicated). When one initiative slips it causes downstream OKR delivery risk and ad-hoc capacity grabs that increase cost and reduce predictability.

Goal: Create an operationally actionable Escalation Matrix and Reserve Capacity Playbook that (1) defines escalation triggers and decision rights across R, A, C, I; (2) codifies a small reserve capacity pool and governed reallocation flows; (3) provides a containment playbook for minimizing customer-facing impact while preserving high-confidence OKR delivery windows.

Scope: Company-level OKRs and cross-functional initiatives for Q2 2026. Not intended to replace team-level sprint triage; instead this is the cross-team arbitration layer for critical-path risks that affect committed company objectives.

Acceptance criteria: 1) Escalation matrix with defined thresholds (slippage days, regression in quality metrics, infra SLO breaches) and named delegates for Level 1/2/3 escalations. 2) Reserve capacity policy documented with budget cap, reallocation approval flow, and rollback criteria. 3) Playbook includes 3 worked examples (runtime kernel regression, Dedicated capacity provisioning delay, Console rollout blocker) with step-by-step actions. 4) Stakeholder sign-off from Eng leadership, Product GTM, and Finance on budgeted reserve. 5) Run a tabletop drill with cross-functional reps and capture learnings.

Key trade-offs considered: 1) Size of reserve pool vs. capital efficiency — we recommend a small (~5-8%) reserved commit for Q2 that can be converted to burst credits if unused. 2) Autonomy vs. central coordination — prefer delegated approvals up to a threshold (48 hours / $X) and Exec-level approval for larger reallocations. 3) Customer-facing fallbacks vs. feature delay — in-situ fallback (model variant downgrade, region fallthrough) preferred for P1 customer-facing outages; feature gating for non-customer impacting regressions.

Stakeholders: Asha Nair (PM lead), Liam Rodriguez (PM owner), Priya Menon (Head Runtime Eng), Mateo Silva (Head Console), Keiko Tanaka (Finance), Security and Legal reviewers.

Artifacts: Draft playbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OKR/Reserve+Capacity+Playbook, Example decision spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ReserveSample, Cost model snapshot in Looker: https://analytics.redwood.ai/dashboards/okr-reserve-capacity.

Next steps: 1) Finalize thresholds and approval delegation by 2026-03-20. 2) Build reserve allocation flow into Console runbooks and tag routes that may be hedged. 3) Schedule tabletop for 2026-03-25 with cross-functional reps.
